topArticle.title: Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds
topArticle.description:
Dozens of Bank of England directors and founding subscribers invested in trafficking of enslaved Africans
The Bank of England and the British financial system were for centuries deeply involved in the enslavement and transatlantic trafficking of millions of African people, according to new research on Britain’s slavery history.
Research by historians compiling the Register of British Slave Traders has found that the scale of the financial system’s involvement in enslavement is greater than previously known or acknowledged. The Bank of England, the central bank owned by the government since nationalisation by Clement Attlee’s Labour administration in 1946, had dozens of financiers involved in its foundation who were also significant investors in the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans.

topArticle.title: ‘Like a Disney movie’: Three wild dog brothers make Africa’s longest journey
topArticle.description:
As three siblings came of age and had to leave their pack, scientists tracked the dogs’ perilous 2,500-mile odyssey to find their own territory
It sounds like a Disney movie: three wild dogs, all brothers, on an epic journey to find a home of their own after their family tells them to leave. They dodge cars and hunters in search of a new life, navigating bushmeat snares and the hostility of a human-dominated landscape until they find a new haven on the African savannah.
But this is exactly what happened in Zambia last year, when three endangered African wild dogs made the longest-ever recorded single journey of any mammal from the continent. The brothers travelled more than 2,500 miles (4,100km) over eight months in their “dispersal” – when a young dog comes of age and must establish new territory to find a mate and start a family of their own.
 Continue reading...

topArticle.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
topArticle.description:
Passionate documentary maker  won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile 
Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.
Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”
 Continue reading...

topArticle.titleJa: ウクライナの郵便局員、ロシアの砲火の下で命の綱を届ける
topArticle.summary: ウクライナの国営郵便サービスは、前線からわずか数マイルの地域に住む人々に年金、薬、手紙を届け、ロシアの砲火の下で命の綱となっている。

topArticle.title: Why a fresh wave of North Korean soldiers may fight in Russia's war in Ukraine
topArticle.description: North Korea will continue to send its soldiers to fight in Russia's war, but only for as long as it is profitable to do so, writes the BBC's Quentin Sommerville.
topArticle.titleJa: なぜ北朝鮮の新たな兵士の波がロシアのウクライナ戦争で戦う可能性があるのか
topArticle.summary: 北朝鮮は利益がある限り、ロシアのウクライナ戦争に兵士を送り続けるだろうとBBCの特派員が報じている。

topArticle.title: Colombia and Brazil deadliest countries for environmental activists, report says
topArticle.description: The two countries accounted for 52% of killings of environmental activists in 2025, according to Global Witness.
topArticle.titleJa: 報告書によると、コロンビアとブラジルは環境活動家にとって最も危険な国
topArticle.summary: グローバル・ウィットネスの報告書によると、2025年に環境活動家殺害の52%がコロンビアとブラジルで発生。両国は活動家にとって最も危険な国とされている。

topArticle.title: More than a month after Venezuela’s earthquakes: ‘I’m not leaving here until my son is found’
topArticle.description: One month after the two earthquakes, thousands of relatives remain beside the collapsed buildings in La Guaira despite harsh conditions and insufficient support for search efforts.
topArticle.titleJa: ベネズエラ地震から1か月以上：「息子が見つかるまでここを離れない」
topArticle.summary: ベネズエラ地震から1か月以上が経過し、ラ・グアイラでは数千人の親族が劣悪な状況と不十分な支援の中、崩壊した建物のそばに留まり、捜索活動を続けている。

topArticle.title: Trump's response is key as Argentina's Falklands demands get louder
topArticle.description: With Argentina's President Milei promising "winds of change" over the Falklands, will Donald Trump shift his stance on British rule?
topArticle.titleJa: アルゼンチンのフォークランド諸島要求が高まる中、トランプ氏の対応が鍵となる
topArticle.summary: アルゼンチンのミレイ大統領がフォークランド諸島領有権主張を強める中、ドナルド・トランプ氏が英国統治への姿勢を変えるか注目されている。米国の対応が鍵となる。

topArticle.title: Weaponizing citizenship: Silencing dissent in Nicaragua
topArticle.description: In this edition, we examine an authoritarian narrative making the case for denationalization in Nicaragua.
topArticle.titleJa: 市民権の武器化：ニカラグアにおける反対意見の封じ込め
topArticle.summary: ニカラグアでは、権威主義的な政権が市民権を武器化し、異議申し立てを封じ込めるための脱国籍化を正当化する言説が展開されている状況を検証する。

topArticle.title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund
topArticle.description: A new study says climate change was a likely factor in the massive flood on the Nepal-Tibet border last month.
topArticle.titleJa: ネパール、国連気候災害基金から数百万ドル請求へ 新たな洪水研究を根拠に
topArticle.summary: ネパールは、ネパール・チベット国境での大規模洪水が気候変動に起因するとする新たな研究に基づき、国連の気候災害基金に資金請求する方針。

topArticle.title: No fire alarms or sprinklers at Pakistan hospital ward where 14 babies died, report finds
topArticle.description: A firefighter tells the BBC that rescuers had said many doors near the unit were locked, obstructing their route to the babies.
topArticle.titleJa: パキスタン病院の新生児病棟で乳児14人死亡、火災報知器・スプリンクラーなしと報告
topArticle.summary: パキスタンの病院で乳児14人が死亡した病棟に火災報知器やスプリンクラーがなかったことが報告された。救助活動も扉が施錠され妨げられたという。

topArticle.title: Inside Singapore's 'Fort Knox' for city's $2bn dirty money auction
topArticle.description: The BBC goes inside a fortified storage facility to view luxury goods seized by police that are now up for auction.
topArticle.titleJa: シンガポールの「フォートノックス」内部に潜入、20億ドルの汚職マネー競売へ
topArticle.summary: シンガポール警察が押収した20億ドル相当の不正資金関連の高級品が競売にかけられる。その保管施設内部にBBCが潜入した。

topArticle.title: More than 1,000 children dead in Bangladesh measles outbreak
topArticle.description: Until March this year, Bangladesh had made "substantial progress" towards eliminating measles.
topArticle.titleJa: バングラデシュで麻疹が大流行、1000人以上の子どもが死亡
topArticle.summary: バングラデシュで麻疹が大流行し、1000人以上の子どもが死亡した。同国はこれまで麻疹根絶に向けて大きな進展を遂げていた。

topArticle.title: Australian police reject request to reopen missing British girl's cold case
topArticle.description: A man's confession to abducting UK toddler Cheryl Grimmer in Australia was previously thrown out.
topArticle.titleJa: オーストラリア警察、失踪した英国人少女の未解決事件再捜査の要請を却下
topArticle.summary: オーストラリア警察は、同国で失踪した英国人幼児シェリル・グリマーちゃんの未解決事件の再捜査要請を却下した。過去に自白も却下されている。

topArticle.title: Philippines' Duterte seen in person at International Criminal Court for first time
topArticle.description: He is due to be tried for crimes against humanity over thousands of deaths linked to his war on drugs.
topArticle.titleJa: フィリピンのドゥテルテ氏、国際刑事裁判所に初出廷
topArticle.summary: フィリピンのドゥテルテ前大統領が国際刑事裁判所に初めて出廷した。「麻薬戦争」に関連する数千人の死を巡る人道に対する罪で裁かれる予定。

topArticle.title: NZ apologises to children forced to live in bush for years with fugitive dad
topArticle.description: A public inquiry has found that agencies "missed key opportunities" to recover the children sooner.
topArticle.titleJa: ニュージーランド、逃亡中の父親と数年間森で暮らした子どもたちに謝罪
topArticle.summary: ニュージーランド政府は、逃亡中の父親と長年森で生活することを強いられた子どもたちに謝罪。公的機関が早期保護の機会を逸したことが判明した。

topArticle.title: Madagascar Launches Safeguard Investigation on Certain Types of Rice
topArticle.description: On 2 September 2026, Madagascar notified the WTO’s Committee on Safeguards that it had initiated on 31 August 2026 a safeguard investigation on imports of hulled rice, semi-whitened or whitened rice, polished or glazed, and broken rice.
topArticle.titleJa: マダガスカル、特定の種類の米に対するセーフガード調査を開始
topArticle.summary: マダガスカルは2026年8月31日、精米、半精米、精白米、砕米の輸入に対するセーフガード調査を開始したことをWTOに通知した。
